flags.detail: QCOM fell a further -2.60% today (to $151.59), extending Wednesday's post-earnings decline. flags.headline: CAT's unexplained -6.97% decline now identified: Baird downgrade on data-center construction moratorium risk
flags.detail: Baird analyst Mircea Dobre downgraded CAT to Neutral from Outperform on 2026-07-29, cutting the price target to $900 from $1,200 (-25%), citing New York Governor Hochul's Executive Order No. 62 (signed 2026-07-14) -- the first statewide moratorium on hyperscale (50MW+) data-center construction -- as the leading edge of a broader wave of 300+ state bills targeting data-center construction, water use, and energy use nationally. Baird's thesis: CAT's Power & Energy segment (engines/generators for data centers) faces a demand air-pocket from 2027 onward. CAT rebounded +3.32% today with the broad market tape but remains well below its pre-downgrade level. This is a real, emerging risk not currently captured in CAT's IOWN report key_risks (which cite cyclical/valuation risk, not data-center regulatory risk) -- worth flagging to the screening side for the next report refresh.

flags.headline: HOOD -3.29%, giving back yesterday's post-earnings gain as crypto-revenue weakness offsets prediction-market strength
flags.detail: Q2 2026 revenue $1.31B (+32% YoY) beat consensus, with event-contract (prediction market) revenue +10x YoY to $156M -- now exceeding both equities and crypto revenue lines, confirming yesterday's headline. But crypto revenue itself fell sharply YoY, and several analysts trimmed price targets post-print even while maintaining bullish ratings (Needham to $120, Barclays to $105, Goldman to $118) on that crypto-revenue softness. Source reporting on the exact earnings date and EPS is inconsistent across outlets (7/29 vs 7/30, and EPS figures of 48c vs 62c both cited) -- treat those specific figures with caution.

flags.headline: COIN Q2 revenue miss and GAAP loss, obscured today by the broad relief rally
flags.detail: Coinbase reported Q2 2026 revenue of $1.22B, down from $1.50B YoY and below consensus (~$1.29-1.35B), with a GAAP loss of $1.36/share versus a much smaller expected loss. Shares fell ~5-6% after-hours on 7/30; today's data drop shows COIN +2.02%, meaning the broad-market rally is masking the company-specific miss rather than the market re-rating it positively. Barclays cut its price target to $95 from $99 (Underweight maintained) shortly after the print. Positives: record ~10.3% crypto-trading volume share and prediction-market revenue >$100M annualized (+2x QoQ).
flags.thesis_link: Matches COIN key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in crypto trading volumes makes Coinbase a leveraged bet on crypto market sentiment, with Q1 2026 revenue down 21% QoQ demonstrating the volatility inherent in the model' -- Q2's YoY revenue decline and GAAP loss is a continuation of this pattern.
